chunks: The illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh the jurist (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from his father. He said: I asked Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the middle night of Sha'ban.

He said: It is a night in which Allah frees the necks from the Fire and forgives major sins in it. I said: Are there any extra prayers in it beyond the rest of the nights? So he said: There is nothing prescribed in it, but if you would like to perform voluntary worship in it with something, then upon you is the prayer of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and increase your remembrance of Allah — Mighty and Majestic — in it, and your seeking of forgiveness and supplication, for indeed my father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Supplication in it is answered.' I said to him: Indeed the people say that it is the night of ordinance. So he (peace be upon him) said: That is the Night of Qadr in the month of Ramadan.

key_terms.صلاة جعفر بن أبي طالب: The Prayer of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib — a recommended voluntary prayer taught by the Prophet to his cousin Ja'far al-Tayyar
key_terms.ليلة الصكاك: The Night of Ordinance — a night erroneously conflated with mid-Sha'ban, correctly identified by the Imam as the Night of Qadr in Ramadan
key_terms.ليلة النصف من شعبان: The middle night of Sha'ban — the 15th night of the month of Sha'ban, widely observed as a night of spiritual significance

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 15th night of Sha'ban according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal asks Imam al-Rida (AS) about the significance of the 15th night of Sha'ban (Laylat al-Nisf min Sha'ban). The Imam explains it is a night of divine mercy when Allah frees souls from Hellfire and forgives major sins. While no specific obligatory prayer is prescribed, the Imam recommends performing the voluntary Prayer of Ja'far al-Tayyar, along with abundant remembrance, seeking forgiveness, and supplication. He also clarifies that the commonly confused 'Night of Ordinance' (Laylat al-Sikak) actually refers to the Night of Qadr (Laylat al-Qadr) in the month of Ramadan, not the night of mid-Sha'ban.
